name: Aero L-29 Delfin
summary: Czech-built jet trainer that served as the standard Eastern Bloc trainer for 40 years and the most common ex-military jet in US private hands.

wings: Straight, mid-set wing with rounded tips
Wing fences on the upper surface, usually no permanent tip tanks
engines: Single turbojet, with intakes on each side of the fuselage just ahead of the wing
One large tailpipe at the rear
fuselage: Pot-bellied, dolphin-like fuselage with a rounded belly
Two tandem bubble canopies with the rear seat raised
Retractable tricycle gear with a tall nose leg
tail: Swept-back fin with a short, rounded tip
Horizontal tail mounted mid-way on the fuselage

tellTales: Rounded, pot-bellied fuselage with a straight mid-mounted wing
Separate tandem canopies and side intakes like a miniature MiG
Straight (not swept) wings and a single big tailpipe

confusedWith.howToTell: The L-39 has a slimmer, straighter fuselage, a more tapered wing and usually wingtip tanks; the L-29 is rounder with a pot belly and no tip tanks.
The Iskra has a longer, narrower fuselage with wing-root intakes and tip tanks; the L-29 has fuselage-side intakes and a bulbous belly.
The T-33 has large tip tanks and a long canopy; the L-29 has two separate canopies and no tip tanks.
